ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a large triangle PQR, with P at the lower left, R at the lower right, Q above, and M on the base PR; segment QM connects downward from Q to M, and a right angle is marked at M, indicating that QM is perpendicular to PR; side PQ is labeled as 13, and segment QM is labeled as 12. Reasoning: In right triangle PQM, PQ is the hypotenuse, QM=12, PQ=13, so PM=sqrt(13^2-12^2)=sqrt(169-144)=5. It is known that triangle PQM is similar to triangle PRQ, with the corresponding order P↔P, Q↔R, M↔Q, so PM corresponds to PQ, PQ corresponds to PR, and QM corresponds to RQ. Since PM=5 corresponds to PQ=13 in the large triangle, the scale factor is 13/5. Thus PR=PQ·13/5=13·13/5=169/5, RQ=QM·13/5=12·13/5=156/5. The perimeter of triangle PQR is PQ+PR+RQ=13+169/5+156/5=13+65=78.

raw_record.question_text: Find the perimeter of $\triangle PQR$, if $\triangle PQM \sim \triangle PRQ$.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a large triangle PQR with M on PR, QM perpendicular to PR, PQ labeled 13, and QM labeled 12. First use the right triangle PQM from the image: since PQ is the hypotenuse and QM=12, compute PM by the Pythagorean theorem as sqrt(13^2-12^2)=5. From the text, use the stated similarity ΔPQM ∼ ΔPRQ with vertex correspondence P↔P, Q↔R, M↔Q. Therefore PM corresponds to PQ, PQ corresponds to PR, and QM corresponds to RQ. The scale factor from ΔPQM to ΔPRQ is PQ/PM=13/5. Use it to get PR=(13)(13/5)=169/5 and RQ=(12)(13/5)=156/5. Add PQ+PR+RQ to get the perimeter.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a right-triangle altitude configuration: Q is the right-angle vertex of the large triangle PQR, M is the foot of the altitude to hypotenuse PR, PQ=13, and QM=12. Use right triangle PQM to find PM=sqrt(13^2-12^2)=5. Then, instead of setting up the full similarity scale factor, use the altitude-to-hypotenuse relation from the similar right triangles: QM^2=PM·MR. Thus 12^2=5·MR, so MR=144/5, and PR=PM+MR=5+144/5=169/5. Use the leg projection relation PQ^2=PM·PR as a check or use the Pythagorean theorem on ΔPQR to find QR=sqrt(PR^2-PQ^2)=156/5. Add PQ+QR+PR to get 78.

推理：在直角三角形 PQM 中，PQ 是斜边，QM = 12，PQ = 13，所以 PM = sqrt(13^2 - 12^2) = sqrt(169 - 144) = 5。由于这是直角三角形 PQR 中从直角 Q 到斜边 PR 的高，使用高到斜边关系：QM^2 = PM · MR。代入得 12^2 = 5 · MR，所以 MR = 144/5。于是 PR = PM + MR = 5 + 144/5 = 169/5。再在直角三角形 PQR 中用勾股定理求 QR：QR = sqrt(PR^2 - PQ^2) = sqrt((169/5)^2 - 13^2) = sqrt(28561/25 - 4225/25) = sqrt(24336/25) = 156/5。因此周长为 PQ + QR + PR = 13 + 156/5 + 169/5 = 78。
